title: Fallout: New Vegas
provenance: Reported by matthiasseghers (highball-db#211, 2026-09-25), Apple M3 Pro, macOS 27.0, Highball 0.9.35, engine x64-crossover26.3-r11, DXVK, AVX advertised, rated 2 of 5: the main menu holds 40 to 50 fps and drops under 10 with lag spikes when hovering menu items. The Wine 10 engine launched worse for them. Not verified by the maintainer. Follow-up 2026-09-28 by the same reporter: DXMT mode on r11, which sends Direct3D 9 to Wine's own Direct3D (the log confirms it), starts smoother and lags less in the menu, but menu and game stay under about 15 fps by their estimate, no counter would show.
notes: A Direct3D 9 game from 2010. On the Wine 11 engines DXVK's Direct3D 9 runs at about half the speed the default engine's does (Five Nights at Freddy's, 40 against 76 fps, measured 2026-09-25). Wine's own Direct3D on r11 helped the reporter but did not make it playable, so the CPU side is the next suspect. Engine r12 adds a patch that speeds up x87 floating point math under Rosetta (Half-Life 2 went from about 131 to 174 fps here), untested with this game. Nothing was measured here.

knownIssues.symptom: Under 10 fps with lag spikes in the main menu on the Wine 11 engine r11 with DXVK, and under about 15 fps (estimated) with Wine's own Direct3D there (M3 Pro, macOS 27.0, highball-db#211).
knownIssues.cause: not measured on this game. DXVK's Direct3D 9 is slow on that tree in general (highball#198's measurements).
knownIssues.fix: none confirmed. Wine's own Direct3D on r11 (the DXMT mode from Highball 0.9.38) helped but was not enough. To try next: engine r12 in the DXMT mode, for its x87 patch.
